host.environment: dedicated Boat managed VM, size large (8 vCPU / 16 GiB RAM)

targets.nanosp: Nano S+, app built with -mcpu=cortex-m35p+nodsp, kernel IR triple thumbv8m.main-none-eabi
targets.nanox: Nano X, app built with -mcpu=cortex-m3, kernel IR triple thumbv6m-none-eabi

commands: bash b1_build.sh   # both trees at one build path, every variant built twice
t7_abba.py prepare --baseline art/ref --candidate art/lean --client-root src/app-bitcoin --profile testnet-perf --output run1 --build-evidence build_evidence.json

report_script_before_run.attestation: self-declared: written by b1_run.sh on the VM before the first launch, not by a third party

limitations: A 14-launch pilot of the same harness ran before the measured run to check that it starts and to size the run; its samples were discarded and were not compared between the two ELFs.

The hub Python environment lacked base58, which the upstream test_utils import; base58 2.1.1 was installed from PyPI into a side directory on the VM. It is client-side only and identical for both ELFs.
The x86_64 rdtscp hotspot table and the host unit-test timings of the previous file are not reproduced here: neither is a measurement of a device ELF.

The four frozen ELF binaries are not committed (the repository ignores *.elf). Their SHA-256 are in frozen_elfs and in manifest.json, and every build was reproduced bit for bit on the VM from the listed commits.
